title: Sunflower spirals intersect isogonally, rarely orthogonally

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Sunflower spirals intersect isogonally, rarely orthogonally

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Against Church, the spirals in a sunflower disc intersect isogonally (at a constant angle), and orthogonal intersection is only a particular and probably infrequent case.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. XIV: On Leaf-Arrangement, or Phyllotaxis

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: The spirals intersect isogonally, but orthogonal intersection would be only one particular case, and in all probability a very infrequent one, in the intersection of logarithmic spirals developed about a common pole.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter XIV, “On Leaf-Arrangement, or Phyllotaxis”; topic “Church's theory of phyllotaxis”. Scope: parastichies in sunflower capitula and similar inflorescences

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch14-02: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.86

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Intersection angles are directly measurable and sharply distinguish isogonal from orthogonal patterns. Large public image sources and straightforward image analysis make the prediction resolvable now.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Extract opposing parastichy families from calibrated sunflower images and measure their local intersection angles across each disc and among heads. Approximate constancy away from 90 degrees supports the claim; systematic angle variation or frequent orthogonality refutes it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Parastichy tracing can be ambiguous near the disc center and edge.

Herbarium images may distort three-dimensional capitula.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.8
analysis feasibility: 0.9
data adequacy: 0.7
discriminating power: 0.95
operationalizability: 0.98

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Intersection angle is directly measurable on the annotated sunflower images already released with the citizen-science counts. Hundreds of heads are enough to estimate how often the crossing is orthogonal and whether the angle stays constant across a disc. Other inflorescences are outside this file, but the claim is aimed at the sunflower case Church discussed, and that case can be decided with the existing images.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: On annotated sunflower discs, measure the angle at which clockwise and anticlockwise parastichies meet at many radii. Isogonal intersection is confirmed if that angle is constant within heads and orthogonal crossing is uncommon across heads; a concentration of intersection angles at 90° would support Church's special case instead.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The open images are domesticated sunflower heads, not a sample of other capitula.

Disordered regions of some heads do not define a single intersection angle.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.72
data existence: 0.88
discriminating power: 0.86
analysis feasibility: 0.85
operationalizability: 0.9
